projects.headline: On the Digilent Nexys A7-100T (xc7a100tcsg324-1, Vivado 2026.1) the on-chip checker caught all 6 seeded protocol bugs on the board, each by the rule it breaks, and the board's traffic matched simulation cycle for cycle in 13 of 13 runs.

hero.caption: Captured on the board: our peripheral, with its early-response bug switched on, raises BVALID after the address handshake but before any write data. The checker flags B_EARLY in that cycle and triggers this capture; the data arrives later.

captions: AW handshake: the address is accepted
BVALID is high but no W handshake has happened: the checker flags B_EARLY and triggers this capture
still flagged: BVALID waits while the write data has not arrived
W handshake: the data arrives, after the response; still flagged: BVALID waits while the write data has not arrived
B handshake: the master takes the early response

next: Full AXI4 with IDs and a DMA target, and a soak mode that steers random traffic towards untested combinations.
Decode the AMD checker's status bits to rule names, and read the counters faster than the serial link allows.
not_measured: Full AXI4 (bursts, IDs, outstanding transactions), the slave side and a long soak: the next phase.
Runs against AMD's BRAM controller are compared with the transaction model, not cycle for cycle with simulation: the simulator used cannot run the AMD core.
The proofs are bounded, and the property restatement shares its author with the checker; the AMD checker is the independent check.

agent.plan: An AI executor (Claude Code) built the AXI4-Lite and AXI4-Stream phase from the planner's brief: the transactor, the rule monitors written from the specification in its own words, formal proofs and checker mutants, a cocotb model driven by the same host code, and a board demonstration with seeded bugs and an AMD checker as an independent cross-check.
agent.request: The owner asked for an on-chip AMBA AXI transactor and analyser that exercises on-chip modules with transactions of any complexity while verifying protocol correctness.

story.how: A transaction program, written in plain YAML and loaded over the serial link, drives AXI4-Lite and AXI4-Stream traffic with seeded random addresses, data, strobes, VALID gaps and READY back-pressure. Port-only monitors check 9 AXI4-Lite and 5 AXI4-Stream rules every cycle, a reference memory checks every read, counters record latency, stalls and coverage, and the first violation triggers a capture. Because every random choice comes from seeded generators, the same program gives the same traffic on the board and in simulation.
story.problem: A bus interface that breaks the AXI handshake rules often works in a quick test and fails in a system: read data that is not held while the master stalls, or a write response sent before the data. Such bugs show only under the right timing, and a logic analyser cannot say which rule was broken.
results: 17 of 17 pre-registered board runs passed. Each of the 6 runs with a seeded protocol bug was flagged by exactly the rule that bug breaks; the 2 runs with a data bug (ignored write strobes, a lost TLAST) were caught by the scoreboard or the stream sink alone; all 9 clean runs fired nothing.

Simulation parity: in 13 of 13 runs against our own peripheral and stream FIFO, the board's checksum over every transaction, latency included, and its cycle count equal the cocotb simulation's; 0 differences in 936 logged transactions.
Cross-check: AMD's AXI Protocol Checker on the same bus asserted in exactly the 5 runs where ours flagged an AXI4-Lite rule; the two verdicts agree in 17 of 17 runs.
The checker itself is proved: 30 of 30 bounded proofs (depth 20) that each rule stays quiet on legal traffic and fires on its own seeded violation, and 34 of 34 deliberately broken checkers caught.
Against AMD's AXI BRAM Controller, write latency ran from 2 to 12 cycles and read latency from 1 to 8 under random back-pressure; 107 reads were checked against the reference memory with no mismatch.

The design used 7089 LUTs, met timing with 0.188 ns of slack and was estimated at 0.189 W; the die stayed at or below 27.32 C and VCCINT within 1.0042 to 1.0071 V, inside the recommended operating conditions, with 0 alarms latched.

projects.one_line: Ask for a capture in words, such as "show me the UART byte when the FIFO overflows": the agent picks the signals by their RTL names, sets the trigger, rebuilds with a logic analyser, captures on the board and answers in plain words beside the waveform.
